concepts.conditions_and_limits: Claims that all approaches work equally well are unwarranted; evaluate evidence and safety.
concepts.application: Identify a trustworthy source of help and an actionable request.
concepts.common_misreading: Treating source anecdotes, metaphors or motivating advice as guaranteed medical or performance outcomes.
concepts.alternative_explanation: Task learning, environmental supports, health, chance and external constraints could contribute without a discrete automatic mechanism.
concepts.ethical_clinical_cautions: Claims that all approaches work equally well are unwarranted; evaluate evidence and safety.
concepts.substantive_paraphrase: The revised-edition discussion connects acceptance of help and personal worth to the larger psycho-cybernetics framework. It presents the premise that the conclusion urges openness to assistance from professionals and other people and rejects unworthiness. It develops this through reduced stigma about accepting support may facilitate action. As an illustration, it describes closing appeals to scientific, religious and interpersonal channels. This is an attributed source argument, not independent evidence of causation; important limitations: Claims that all approaches work equally well are unwarranted; evaluate evidence and safety.
concepts.source_specific_illustration: Closing appeals to scientific, religious and interpersonal channels.
concepts.chapter_argument_role: A chapter-specific step in the argument, anchored to a first-hand read page, not standalone proof.
concepts.evidence_assessment: Book statement verified in original PDF; empirical corroboration not undertaken.
